hook: Deleted in SIR? Re-applying won't get you *prosecuted*, Supreme Court says
tldr: The Supreme Court orally assured that voters deleted in Maharashtra's SIR won't be prosecuted just for re-applying with Form 6; it hears the plea on Nov 5. Separately, the Election Commission told the court the CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge.

beats.what: Petitioners say thousands in Mumbai and Pune were marked absent because their buildings are under redevelopment (3,500 projects in Mumbai, 1,500 in Pune).
beats.why: Fear of prosecution was stopping deleted voters from re-registering.
beats.care: Name missing? Fill Form 6 on voters.eci.gov.in. The court says re-applying alone isn't an offence.

cards.q: Which form do you use to re-register as a voter?
cards.why: Form 6 is for new or re-registration. Form 7 is for deletion.

viz.l: SC hears the Maharashtra SIR plea

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Deleted voters will not be prosecuted for filing Form 6: SC; CEC can be removed only like an SC judge, ECI says (print, Hyderabad edition, 27 Oct, p.9)
